text: In eighteen fifty eight, London smelled so bad... even Parliament wanted to escape.
Back then, the River Thames wasn't just a river. It was London's giant open sewer.
For decades, people dumped human waste, dead animals, and industrial garbage straight into it.
Then came the summer of eighteen fifty eight.
Temperatures soared above thirty degrees Celsius, and the filthy river began baking in the heat.
People couldn't stand near the river. And inside Parliament?
Politicians desperately closed the windows and soaked the curtains in chemicals to block the stench.
There was even talk of moving Parliament.
They rushed through a new law in just eighteen days,
and gave engineer Joseph Bazalgette the green light to build a massive underground sewer system.
It took years to complete, but by eighteen seventy five, London's new sewer network was in place.
The Great Stink didn't just embarrass London.
It forced an entire city to rebuild what was underneath it.
